central_topic: Budgeted selection of a few MTEB embedding tasks to predict a held-out model's unmeasured task scores from a naturally incomplete historical model-by-task matrix, evaluated by absolute prediction error.
core_methods: Observed-data factor-analysis EM with low-rank-plus-diagonal residual covariance and Gaussian conditional prediction
Regularized latent Gaussian mixtures on a fixed factor representation with observation-dependent posterior component weights
Bounded marginal posterior medians for absolute-error prediction
Off-diagonal conditional-covariance transfer selection and a moment-matched standard-deviation-reduction acquisition surrogate
Historical model-heldout tuning on fixed, nonqueryable target tasks
Implemented quadrature-integrated posterior absolute-risk acquisition extension, without a demonstrated aggregate advantage over the retained mixture configuration
comparators: Random task panels with low-rank conditional prediction / matrix completion
Correlation-coverage greedy task selection with ridge prediction
Historical per-task means and observed-score-copy controls
Item-level evaluation compression: tinyBenchmarks and metabench, distinct from selecting whole benchmark tasks
Latent capability and cross-family performance prediction: Observational Scaling Laws and Sloth
Bayesian active feature acquisition and prediction-oriented experimental design as methodological context, not additional evaluated baselines
benchmarks: MTEB embeddings-benchmark/results at revision 6dabbcc68c28ea5f180ce7df79347b3ca9cc6383; local model-by-task panels retain natural missingness

English MTEB task contexts visible in the panels include classification, semantic textual similarity, clustering, and retrieval/reranking; examples include Banking77Classification, STSBenchmark, ArguAna, and AskUbuntuDupQuestions
result_driven_themes: Final aggregate MAE favors the retained latent-mixture-capable system over random low-rank, greedy ridge, and historical-mean controls, without isolating the contribution of individual mechanisms
The loss increase under columnwise permutation supports dependence on cross-task score structure rather than marginal task means alone; it does not establish causal transfer
Model-group and family-disjoint evaluations motivate discussion of generalization, with family labels limited to name-derived lineage proxies rather than verified architectural ancestry
Absolute-error evaluation motivates posterior-median prediction and loss-aligned acquisition, but mechanism-specific gains are not independently established
Fixed nonqueryable audit targets matter because acquiring a task removes its error from the changing-complement metric

The quadrature extension matches the retained mixture configuration's aggregate search MAE; neither quadrature superiority nor actual deployment of a particular mixture size is established by aggregate results

queries.query: factor analysis expectation maximization missing observations diagonal residual covariance
queries.rationale: The retained predictor fits a low-rank-plus-diagonal Gaussian model using observed entries and latent posterior moments, rather than treating imputed cells as labels. Seek original methodological sources for that likelihood and conditioning framework.

queries.query: mixtures of factor analyzers missing data latent Gaussian mixture
queries.rationale: The retained configuration extends a fixed factor representation with a regularized latent Gaussian mixture and observation-dependent responsibilities. Mixtures of factor analyzers are a relevant parent family, not an exact description of this shared-loading/shared-residual implementation.

queries.query: Bayesian active feature acquisition expected prediction loss experimental design
queries.rationale: Running a task reveals one feature of the new model's score vector. Prediction-oriented acquisition connects off-diagonal transfer, the mixture covariance surrogate, and the implemented quadrature alternative without assuming entropy reduction or MAE-optimality.

queries.query: low rank matrix completion collaborative filtering matrix factorization
queries.rationale: A naturally incomplete model-by-task score matrix and the measured random-panel low-rank baseline imply matrix-completion and collaborative-filtering comparators. Distinguish recovering historical cells from conditioning predictions for a held-out row with a limited observation budget.

MTEB is the actual evaluated data source. Its task diversity and embedding-model setting define the scientific scope; do not substitute generative-model benchmark evidence for these experiments. This is a permitted starter title.

This permitted starter work anchors item-level evaluation compression, an expected related-work comparison that must be distinguished from selecting whole MTEB tasks. It was not run as an experimental baseline.

queries.query: "metabench" "A Sparse Benchmark of Reasoning and Knowledge in Large Language Models"
queries.rationale: This permitted starter work addresses sparse multi-benchmark evaluation and score reconstruction. It is a close conceptual comparator, while its sampled-item unit and reasoning/knowledge setting differ from the observed embedding-task panels.

queries.query: "Observational Scaling Laws and the Predictability of Language Model Performance"
queries.rationale: This permitted starter work situates predictive low-dimensional structure in historical model evaluations. The present run uses score observations rather than demonstrating a compute-scaling law.

queries.query: "Sloth: scaling laws for LLM skills to predict multi-benchmark performance across families"
queries.rationale: This permitted starter work directly motivates comparison with latent-skill and across-family prediction literature. Local family-disjoint tests use name-defined proxies and do not establish architectural transfer or equivalence to skill scaling laws.

queries.query: Bayesian decision theory posterior median absolute error loss
queries.rationale: MAE is the measured objective and bounded posterior medians are implemented. Foundational decision-theoretic grounding distinguishes optimal actions under the fitted distribution from guaranteed real-data error reductions; no isolated median-versus-mean advantage is claimed.
